# Known double-free-shape rows, reviewed and tolerated.
#
# Format: <Class>|<File>
# Generated by tools/scan_double_free.py. Each row was read and classified:
#   CRenderClip        stack-scoped RAII clip; copying it WOULD double-DeleteObject.
#                      Kept in the baseline because the fix is to make it non-copyable,
#                      which is queued, not because it is safe.
#   CActiveXCtrl       always heap-allocated via new and owned by one control.
#   MenuObserverImpl   created via new in CMenuWnd; pReceivers_ deleted in its dtor.
#   MenuReceiverImpl   same pattern.
#
# Removing a row records that the class was actually fixed.
#
# Removed in round 57 (explicit = delete on copy ops):
#   CControlUI|UIControl.h        CContainerUI|UIContainer.h
#   CPaintManagerUI|UIManager.h
# Removed in round 58 (non-copyable by inheritance / false positive on non-owning
# back-pointers): CLoadingUI, CGifAnimExUI, CColorPaletteUI, CRichEditUI,
# CActiveXEnum, CActiveXFrameWnd, CDragSourceHelper, CIDropTarget, CSafeRelease,
# CTxtWinHost, TUnzip(unzip.cpp, vendored).

# Round 59: the three rows removed above were cleared after
# tools/scan_byvalue_use.py proved they have no by-value use anywhere in DuiLib/ or
# Demos/ (pointer/reference only, plus one function-local static returned by
# reference). The evidence is a command, not a note:
#     python tools/scan_byvalue_use.py --class CActiveXCtrl --class MenuObserverImpl --class MenuReceiverImpl
# If that command ever reports a hit, the class is a real risk again and its row
# must come back.
